unit: Ch 2: Audit Strategy, Audit Planning and Audit Programme
note: AI-written summary of ICAI study material. Check the original for exact wording.

topics.title: Auditor's Responsibility & Benefits of Audit Planning
explain: SA 300 states that the objective of the auditor is to plan the audit so that it will be performed in an effective, efficient, and timely manner.
Planning helps reduce audit risk to an acceptably low level, minimizing the chance of expressing an inappropriate audit opinion.

Benefits of planning include focusing attention on key areas, timely resolution of potential problems, proper organization of the engagement, assignment of competent team members, proper supervision, and coordinating work with experts.
Audit planning is not a one-time discrete phase; it is a continuous and iterative process starting shortly after the previous audit finishes and continuing through the current audit.
Key engagement team members, including the partner, must participate in planning to utilize their experience and insights.
The auditor may discuss elements of planning with management for better coordination, provided it does not compromise audit effectiveness or the element of surprise.

flow.title: Continuous Audit Planning Process
steps: Complete previous year audit engagement
Initiate preliminary planning activities
Assess risks of material misstatement
Develop detailed audit plan
Update planning decisions throughout audit

topics.example: An auditor plans to visit a factory during inventory counting at year-end so that team members with stock verification experience are assigned to high-value locations on time.
remember: Planning is continuous and iterative, not a discrete one-time event.
mistakes: Thinking that discussing planning timing with management automatically compromises audit secrecy. (Only sharing specific unannounced procedure details compromises audit effectiveness).

quiz.q: According to SA 300, which of the following statements correctly describes audit planning?
o: It is a discrete phase that finishes before fieldwork begins.
It is a continuous and iterative process throughout the audit.
It is sole responsibility of the client's management.
It cannot be modified once documented.
quiz.why: SA 300 emphasizes that audit planning is a continuous and iterative process that runs until the completion of the audit engagement.

quiz.q: Which of the following is NOT a benefit of audit planning?
o: Helping the auditor devote appropriate attention to important areas
Assisting in selecting competent engagement team members
Guaranteeing that zero misstatements exist in financial statements
Facilitating timely identification and resolution of potential problems
quiz.why: Planning reduces audit risk to an acceptable low level but cannot guarantee zero misstatements in financial statements.

topics.title: Preliminary Engagement Activities
explain: Before starting major planning activities, the auditor must complete preliminary engagement activities.
Preliminary activities assist in identifying events or circumstances that could adversely affect the auditor's ability to plan and perform the audit.
Step 1: Perform client continuance procedures to check management integrity, team competence, and communicate with predecessor auditors for initial engagements.
Step 2: Evaluate compliance with ethical requirements including independence throughout the engagement.
Step 3: Establish a clear understanding of the engagement terms by issuing an audit engagement letter to prevent misunderstandings.

flow.title: Executing Preliminary Engagement Activities
steps: Evaluate client continuance and management integrity
Verify engagement team competence and capability
Check compliance with ethical and independence rules
Communicate with predecessor auditor if initial audit
Issue audit engagement letter to client

topics.example: Before accepting the audit of a new manufacturing firm, the audit partner contacts the previous auditor to inquire about any professional reasons why the audit should not be accepted.
remember: Preliminary activities consist of: Client continuance, Ethical/Independence checks, and Engagement letter terms.
mistakes: Assuming preliminary engagement activities happen after drafting the detailed audit plan. (They must occur before detailed planning activities).

quiz.q: Which of the following is included under preliminary engagement activities?
o: Designing detailed audit procedures for inventory
Evaluating compliance with ethical requirements including independence
Drafting the final audit report
Submitting tax return filings for the client
quiz.why: Evaluating compliance with ethical requirements and independence is one of the three main preliminary engagement activities.

quiz.q: Why does an auditor issue an audit engagement letter before commencing the audit?
o: To guarantee an unqualified opinion
To establish mutual understanding of engagement terms and avoid confusion
To shift audit responsibility to third-party experts
To fix final tax liabilities of the entity
quiz.why: The engagement letter documents terms of engagement to avoid misunderstandings between the auditor and the client.

topics.title: Overall Audit Strategy and Detailed Audit Plan
explain: Overall audit strategy sets the scope, timing, and direction of the audit, guiding the development of the detailed audit plan.
Establishing audit strategy helps determine resource deployment: who to deploy (experts/experienced staff), how much resource to allocate, when to deploy them, and how to supervise them.

Key factors considered when framing strategy: scope characteristics (FRF, segment needs), reporting objectives (timelines, meeting schedules), significant factors (transaction volume, industry changes), preliminary activity results, and required resource details.
The Audit Plan is more detailed than the overall audit strategy.
The audit plan includes descriptions of: (1) Planned risk assessment procedures, (2) Planned further audit procedures at the assertion level, and (3) Other planned procedures required by SAs.
Strategy and audit plan are closely inter-related; a change in strategy leads to a consequential change in the plan.

flow.title: Developing Strategy and Audit Plan
steps: Identify scope FRF and reporting objectives
Evaluate significant factors and preliminary results
Determine nature timing extent of resources
Formulate overall audit strategy
Draft detailed audit plan for procedures

topics.example: If a company operates in a highly regulated telecom sector under TRAI regulations, the auditor includes compliance with TRAI norms in the overall audit strategy, requiring specialized compliance audit procedures in the audit plan.
remember: Audit Strategy sets scope, timing, and direction.
Audit Plan details nature, timing, and extent of planned procedures.
mistakes: Believing that establishing overall strategy and audit plan are completely separate, sequential steps. (They are closely inter-related and overlap).

quiz.q: What is the primary role of the overall audit strategy?
o: To list daily attendance of audit assistants
To set the scope, timing, and direction of the audit
To replace substantive checking with internal controls
To finalize book adjustments prior to audit start
quiz.why: The overall audit strategy sets the scope, timing, and direction of the audit and guides the development of the audit plan.

quiz.q: Which of the following must be included in an audit plan under SA 300?
o: Planned risk assessment procedures
Planned further audit procedures at assertion level
Other planned audit procedures required for SA compliance
All of the above
quiz.why: SA 300 requires the audit plan to describe risk assessment procedures, further audit procedures, and other procedures necessary to comply with SAs.

topics.title: Auditor's Responsibility, Changes, Supervision, and Documentation
explain: The overall audit strategy and detailed audit plan remain the sole responsibility of the statutory auditor.
Management cannot be tasked with preparing the audit strategy or audit plan; delegating this compromises audit effectiveness.
Audit planning is flexible: the auditor must update and change the strategy and plan during the audit whenever unexpected events, changed conditions, or contradictory evidence emerge.
The nature, timing, and extent of direction, supervision, and review of team members depend on entity size/complexity, audit area, assessed risks of material misstatement, and team competence.
Documentation requirements under SA 300: Auditor must document (1) Overall audit strategy, (2) Audit plan, and (3) Any significant changes made during the audit along with reasons.

flow.title: Managing Strategy Changes and Documentation
steps: Establish initial strategy and plan
Execute audit procedures and observe findings
Identify unexpected events or contradictory evidence
Modify audit strategy and plan accordingly
Document strategy plan and reasons for changes

topics.example: While checking sales invoices, the auditor finds widespread internal control breakdowns. The auditor modifies the audit plan by increasing sample sizes and shifting from control testing to detailed substantive testing, documenting the reasons for this change.
remember: Auditor alone is responsible for audit strategy and plan.
Document strategy, plan, and ALL significant changes with reasons.
mistakes: Assuming planning decisions cannot be changed once the audit starts. (Auditors must update strategy and plan when new facts emerge).

quiz.q: If an auditor delegates the preparation of the overall audit strategy to the client's head of finance, what is the consequence?
o: Audit efficiency increases without any non-compliance.
It is proper as per SA 300.
The auditor fails their responsibility, compromising audit effectiveness.
It is mandatory for listed company audits.
quiz.why: Establishing the audit strategy is the auditor's sole responsibility; delegating it to client management compromises audit effectiveness.

quiz.q: What must the auditor document regarding audit planning under SA 300?
o: Only the initial engagement letter
Overall audit strategy, audit plan, and significant changes with reasons
Only the final audit report
Personal notes of junior assistants
quiz.why: SA 300 explicitly mandates documenting the overall strategy, audit plan, and any significant changes made with reasons.

topics.title: Audit Programme - Concept, Construction & Evidence
explain: An audit programme is a detailed, written plan of verification steps and instructions to be applied to financial statements and accounting records to obtain sufficient appropriate audit evidence.
A single standard audit programme cannot be used for all businesses because entities vary in size, nature, internal controls, and operations.

Key points when constructing an audit programme: Stay within assignment scope, prepare written procedures, identify available evidence, apply useful steps, include area objectives, consider error possibilities, and coordinate related items.
Audit evidence includes documentary examination, physical checks, management/third-party statements, calculations, control evaluations, accounting data inter-relationships, and minutes.
'Available evidence' refers to evidence that normally should be available under business circumstances, not just what the client presents.

flow.title: Constructing an Audit Programme
steps: Stay within scope and assignment limits
Identify audit objectives for each area
Determine reasonably available audit evidence
Draft written procedures and specific instructions
Coordinate verification steps for related items

topics.example: To verify cash in hand, the best audit evidence prescribed in the audit programme is physical count, whereas for investments pledged with a bank, a banker's certificate is prescribed.
remember: One uniform audit programme is NOT practicable for all businesses.
Audit evidence is broader than just client-provided documents.
mistakes: Assuming 'available evidence' means relying solely on whatever documents the client chooses to produce. (The auditor must seek evidence that normally ought to exist).

quiz.q: Why is a single audit programme NOT practicable for all businesses?
o: Because audit fees differ for every business
Because businesses vary in size, nature, composition, and internal controls
Because SAs prohibit written audit programmes
Because junior assistants cannot read standard programmes
quiz.why: Variations in business nature, size, internal control operations, and engagement scope make a single uniform programme impractical.

quiz.q: Which of the following is considered the best audit evidence for verifying cash in hand?
o: Management written representation
Physical cash count
Bank ledger entry
Previous year audit file
quiz.why: Physical count provides the highest direct audit evidence for verifying physical assets like cash in hand.

topics.title: Audit Programme: Review, Flexibility, Advantages & Disadvantages
explain: Audit assistants must follow the written audit programme but keep an open mind beyond given steps, reporting significant unexpected matters to seniors.
Periodic review of the audit programme is essential to ensure it stays updated; following an unreviewed, obsolete programme when client business policies change leads to audit negligence liability.

Advantages of an audit programme: Provides clear instructions, gives total perspective for major audits, facilitates work allocation by capability, prevents overlooking records, fixes responsibility via sign-offs, and serves as defense evidence in court.
Purported disadvantages: Work may become mechanical, programme may become rigid/inflexible, inefficient staff may take shelter behind it, and initiative of enterprising staff may be killed.
All disadvantages can be eliminated through imaginative supervision and encouraging assistants to observe matters objectively.

flow.title: Periodic Review and Application of Programme
steps: Issue standard written audit programme
Assistants execute steps keeping open mind
Observe changes in client business policies
Perform periodic review of the programme
Update procedures to prevent audit negligence

topics.example: A company switches from physical sales to an e-commerce platform. The auditor must review and update the audit programme to include digital payment verification instead of relying on old manual sales checking steps.
remember: Periodic review of audit programme prevents audit negligence liability.
Disadvantages of audit programme are eliminated by imaginative supervision.
mistakes: Believing that audit assistants should strictly ignore unexpected findings if they are not written in the audit programme. (Assistants must keep an open mind and report unexpected findings).

quiz.q: What is the consequence if an auditor fails to periodically review and update an audit programme despite major changes in the client's business?
o: The audit becomes automatically exempt from SA 300.
The audit work may become obsolete, rendering the auditor liable for negligence.
The audit fee is automatically doubled by law.
Nothing, as old programmes are legally valid forever.
quiz.why: Carrying out audit work on an obsolete programme due to lack of periodic review amounts to negligence for which the auditor faces legal consequences.

quiz.q: How can the disadvantages of an audit programme (like rigidity or mechanical work) be overcome?
o: By eliminating written documentation completely
Through imaginative supervision and encouraging assistants to keep an open mind
By letting client management draft the audit steps
By reducing audit sample sizes to zero
quiz.why: Imaginative supervision and encouraging team members to think objectively eliminate the rigidity and mechanical nature of audit programmes.
